coursesExamined.name: Personal & Professional Development
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides mandatory first-year source evaluation, communication, reflection and civic formation; it is not an organisational research placement

coursesExamined.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces financial accounting, management accounting and investment appraisal, including accounting's social role and accountability implications. Students record transactions, prepare and interpret financial statements, and analyze performance and financing. The course then examines costing, pricing, budgeting, organizational control and sustainable management accounting. Investment decisions are evaluated using accounting and discounted-cash-flow measures. A case study analyzes the misuse of an accounting principle and its financial-statement effects.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides complementary financial-statement and accounting analysis; healthcare budgets or hospital logistics are not required applications
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Economics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces microeconomic principles and short-run macroeconomic analysis. The microeconomic component examines supply and demand, strategic interaction, consumer choice, production, costs and competitive markets. The macroeconomic component introduces output, unemployment and inflation, then relates goods and financial markets through the IS-LM model. Students use algebra and graphs to explain economic behaviour and apply models to economic issues.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides complementary microeconomic/macroeconomic concepts for analysing markets and allocation, without specialised health-insurance teaching
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.

coursesExamined.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops microeconomic theory through consumer behaviour, imperfectly competitive markets and economy-wide allocation. Students examine choice under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations, then monopoly, strategic behaviour and labour and capital markets. General equilibrium, efficiency, externalities and government complete the analysis. Algebraic problem-solving and graphical analysis are connected to the interpretation and evaluation of research papers.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides complementary consumer/producer theory, uncertainty, imperfect competition, factor markets, efficiency and government intervention; medical insurance is not a required case
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.

coursesExamined.name: Public Economics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines government intervention through the efficiency and equity effects of public policy. Market failure, public goods and externalities provide foundations for studying public production, collective choice, spending and taxation. Health, education, welfare and social insurance illustrate expenditure and redistribution questions. Students apply economic models, interpret data and graphs, evaluate research and develop a research proposal and paper.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.
coursesExamined.contribution: Studies public goods, market failure, taxation, spending and redistribution, with explicit health, education, welfare and social-insurance applications. Models, data, research appraisal and a paper/proposal provide allocation tools; this is not Dutch insurance-law training.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

coursesExamined.name: Econometrics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. coursesExamined.name: Consumer Product Design
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Teaches consumer-product design and development through projects that progress from understanding an existing product to creating a new one. Students investigate product mechanisms and environmental impact, interview potential customers, translate needs into specifications, select concepts, and develop production plans and prototypes where feasible. The final project integrates these stages with industrial scaling and elementary economic analysis. Sustainability, including material use, repairability, lifespan and circularity, informs design decisions throughout.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.
coursesExamined.contribution: Develops customer needs, specifications, concept selection, production plans and prototypes where feasible, with cost, scaling, repairability and circularity considerations. These are product innovation methods; a medical product or healthcare service is not prescribed.

coursesExamined.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Connects marketing strategy and consumer psychology to responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students study strategic planning, customer experience, qualitative and quantitative insights, brand identity, digital marketing and behavioural framing. Applied projects analyze a company's strategy and response to disruption, design a brand, and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Customer-journey mapping translates findings into recommendations.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course unpacks what drives consumer engagement with brands and how marketers build customer trust responsibly. It introduces key marketing concepts, consumer psychology, AI/technology-driven marketing innovation, and brand and communication strategies. Students will explore real-life case studies, develop a strategic marketing plan and learn how marketers build sustainable brand strategies.
coursesExamined.contribution: Studies consumer psychology, customer insights, marketing and responsible brand development. Projects design a brand, investigate strategy/consumer behaviour and map customer journeys. These user/adoption methods complement health-needs inquiry; patient projects are not prescribed.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Marketing & Consumer Engagement examines consumer psychology, marketing strategy, responsible brand development and customer engagement. Students analyse a company strategy, design a brand and investigate a consumer phenomenon using academic literature and primary and secondary evidence. Digital marketing and customer-journey mapping connect analysis with practical recommendations.

coursesExamined.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces entrepreneurship and core business functions through the development of a startup concept. Students use design thinking to discover customer needs, define a problem, generate and prototype solutions, and construct value propositions and business models. Marketing, finance, operations, human resources and funding inform a coherent business plan and investor pitch. Entrepreneurial cases and a startup simulation examine decision-making, early growth and business lifecycles, with attention to societal impact and sustainability.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures. No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

coursesExamined.name: Research Methods & Statistics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Research Methods & Statistics gives you a strong foundation in how business management—and social and behavioral sciences—move from mere practices to true fields of scientific study. You’ll learn how to plan research logically, from designing studies to working with real data using experimental and survey techniques. You’ll also study descriptive and inferential statistics, with a brief intro to multivariate tools.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides complementary general research design and descriptive/inferential statistics, including group research; it is not specialist health-services methodology

coursesExamined.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines organizational behaviour at individual, group and organizational levels. Topics connect personality, perception, emotions and motivation to teams, leadership, power, conflict, structure, culture and change. Students design research plans for organizational cases and conduct a brief systematic literature review using PRISMA reporting tools. Workshops develop literature searching, study selection, source appraisal and synthesis, linking organizational-psychology evidence to practical questions and recommendations.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course offers Liberal Arts and Sciences students a deep dive into the psychological, social, and structural dynamics that shape workplaces. Through interactive case discussions, simulations, and real-world insights, students develop critical skills in motivation, leadership, group dynamics, and culture. By synthesizing research and applying theory to practice, participants gain the tools to navigate and influence diverse organizational environments effectively.

coursesExamined.name: AI Ethics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines AI through ethical theory and psychological accounts of human behaviour and interaction. Ethical debates address fairness, privacy, responsibility, alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Psychological perspectives consider development, clinical care, social and organizational relationships, forensic applications and cognitive neuroscience. Students synthesize literature and apply ethical frameworks in an analytical psychology project and a research-grounded podcast, with a creative communication component.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Explores philosophical foundations and implications of AI. Examines the history of AI, ethical issues like interpretability, bias and alignment, debates about AI consciousness and implications for human nature.
coursesExamined.contribution: Examines fairness, privacy, responsibility, trust and AI ethics alongside psychological perspectives including clinical care, development and social or organisational interaction. coursesExamined.name: Law, Society & Justice
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces law through legal, social and normative perspectives. Students compare major legal traditions and survey public and private law, including constitutional, criminal, international, human-rights, property, contract and tort law. The second part examines justice, social control and change, race and gender. Case briefs, legal interpretation, demand letters and mock trials apply legal reasoning; a family-law topic supports the design of a small socio-legal research proposal.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Examines law from legal, socio‑scientific and normative perspectives. Explores definitions, legal traditions and fields of law, investigates the relationship between law and society and the concept of justice, and includes case law, excursion to international legal organisations, interviews with practitioners and a moot court session.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides complementary legal-system, rights and justice foundations; it is not Dutch healthcare-system or patient-law training

coursesExamined.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies human rights both as positive law and as philosophical claims. Students examine the UDHR, European and UN protection systems, monitoring institutions and landmark cases alongside natural law, natural rights, legal positivism and critiques of universality. Historical and philosophical texts frame debates about dignity, life and reproductive rights, punishment, religious freedom, expression and democracy. Close engagement with legal and philosophical arguments supports independent moral positions.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Offers a legal, historical and philosophical approach to human rights. Studies classical and modern philosophers, traces the rise of human rights, examines the US Bill of Rights and the French Declaration, and discusses human rights treaties.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides complementary legal, historical and philosophical human-rights analysis, without a health-law or patient-rights specialisation

coursesExamined.name: Comparative Constitutional Law

Students examine constitutional features, federalism, legislatures, executive relationships, courts, judicial review and human rights. The administrative component addresses public participation, remedies and procedural fairness. A staged booklet compares two constitutions, supported by legal interpretation, case-law analysis and application of principles to hypothetical facts.

coursesExamined.name: Ethics

coursesExamined.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces empirical comparison of political systems, with democracy, democratization and autocratization as central concerns. Students study political institutions, rules, actors and behaviour, including parties, elections, participation, polarization, interest groups and policy. Research exercises operationalize and measure democracy using V-Dem data and compare academic literature-search tools. A qualitative or quantitative research memo answers a theoretically grounded comparative-politics question through empirical analysis.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Provides analytical tools to compare political systems and democracies. coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Sociology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces sociological reasoning through classical theories, their historical settings and perspectives that address exclusions from the discipline. Students connect solidarity, modernity, identity, social boundaries, networks and stratification to race, gender, migration and inequality in education and work. An individual analysis applies a course concept to contemporary social life without original data collection. A group paper develops a sociological question and analyzes a social problem using theory and academic literature.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces concepts, theories and methods of sociology. Examines socio‑historical context of key authors like Marx, Weber, Durkheim and Du Bois, and encourages exploration of social problems related to race, gender and class through theoretical approaches and methodologies.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides complementary social theory, social institutions and race/gender/class analysis; medical sociology is not required content

coursesExamined.name: Qualitative Research Methodology

Students examine methodological foundations, ethics, positionality and reflexivity alongside interviews, focus groups, ethnography, documentary and visual approaches. Coding, thematic interpretation and NVivo support analysis. Research teams formulate a question, collect and analyze qualitative evidence, and report their methodological decisions, findings and limitations in staged assignments.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces qualitative research methodology. Covers designing questions, interpreting meaning and conducting small team projects, while reflecting on complexity and power dynamics in social research.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides complementary qualitative research design, collection, interpretation, reflexivity and dissemination; no healthcare fieldwork requirement is inferred

Students compare theories and apply them to empirical cases, including visual material. An individual research paper develops a theoretically grounded interpretation of a selected social phenomenon.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Examines the trajectory of sociology within the culture of imperialism and colonial responses. Studies leading social theories and debates about modernity and critically engages with sociological discourses.

coursesExamined.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces epidemiological reasoning and its application to public health. Students measure and interpret disease patterns, study research designs, association, bias, confounding and causality, then examine health determinants, promotion, needs assessment and screening. A local project analyzes a Zeeland health challenge, compares population data, considers affected groups and interventions, and incorporates stakeholder perspectives into feasible recommendations.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead:
Public health is about changing the world. From pandemics to lifestyle-related diseases, from screening for disease to improving water and air quality, it asks: how can we improve to keep the population healthy?_x000D_
But how do we know what actually works? In this course you will dive into epidemiology: the science behind public health. You will learn how to study disease, risks, and changes over time, and how to critically evaluate evidence. Because behind every public health decision lies a question of evidence, and by the end of this course, you will be equipped to engage with it. This course invites you to look beyond the lab, the hospital, and the library, into the wider world where health is shaped. What matters most if we truly care about health, and how can we influence that?
coursesExamined.contribution: directly studies epidemiology, disease risk and patterns, prevention, population health and critical assessment of public-health evidence
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Introduces epidemiology and the evidence used in public health. It examines disease patterns, risks and changes over time, and how research can inform decisions about population health.

A creative assignment constructs an imaginary disease whose symptoms, mechanism and proposed treatment must form a coherent pathophysiological account.

coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Examines how normal organ-system function relates to disease. coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces the molecular and cellular foundations of life and biomedical science. Students study biological molecules, cells and membranes, communication, enzymes and energy metabolism, cell division, DNA and heredity, gene expression, genomes and biotechnology. Scientific experiments and papers are analyzed through short teaching contributions and a research-based mini-symposium. A responsive final component selects additional life- and biomedical-science topics with the class.

coursesExamined.contribution: Develops molecular, cellular and biochemical foundations, genetics and scientific evidence appraisal for disease science; it does not supply complete organ physiology or health policy.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Introduces the molecular and cellular foundations of life and biomedical science. Topics include biological molecules, cells and membranes, communication, metabolism, cell division, heredity, gene expression and biotechnology. Students analyse scientific experiments and papers through teaching contributions and a research-based mini-symposium, with additional topics selected with the class.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces psychological and neuroscientific explanations of behaviour and mental processes. Students study neural signalling, brain anatomy and development, learning, intelligence, personality, social influence, mental disorders and treatments. Several sessions introduce behavioural, imaging and electrophysiological approaches to neuroscience and their combined use. Interdisciplinary research-article and case analysis connects psychological processes to neural mechanisms and clinical questions.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides the psychological/neuroscientific foundation and formal gateway for selected psychology courses; it is not clinical practice training
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.

coursesExamined.name: Social Psychology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces the scientific study of how thoughts, feelings and behaviour are shaped by other people and social situations. Social cognition, the self, influence and persuasion lead into group processes, prejudice, aggression, prosocial behaviour, attraction and close relationships. Students critically examine empirical research, synthesize findings from journal articles, formulate theory-guided questions and design a feasible study. The final project proposes research rather than conducting an empirical investigation.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides complementary social-psychological theories and evidence about the influence of others on thoughts, feelings and behaviour
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.

coursesExamined.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research. Students choose, fit, diagnose and interpret multivariable models, comparing means, analyzing categorical outcomes and studying latent constructs. R, primarily through R Commander, supports repeated practical exercises; SPSS is an optional alternative. Data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions and hypotheses to appropriate models, assumption checks, substantive interpretation and APA reporting.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: The course is necessary for students who want to pursue master programs in psychology and adjacent disciplines, as well as research masters in the medical domain. It is highly recommended also for all those who want to be researchers in other domains. In addition to technical training, the course emphasizes clear academic communication. It will equip you with the skills necessary to apply advanced statistical techniques to real-world research problems. With a focus on practical application through case studies and data analysis projects, You will be able to choose the appropriate statistical model for various research scenarios and address common challenges in data interpretation.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides multivariate statistics, regression, factor analysis, (co)variance analysis and non-parametric methods for empirical research; it is not health-economics evaluation
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research. Students choose, fit, diagnose and interpret multivariable models for group comparisons, categorical outcomes and latent constructs. R, primarily through R Commander, supports practical exercises; data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions to appropriate models, assumption checks and clear reporting.

coursesExamined.name: Psychopathology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines mental health and psychopathology across the lifespan using a biopsychosocial perspective. Historical views, classification and assessment frame biological, psychological, cultural and social explanations of disorders and treatment. Case-based work applies diagnostic concepts to varied presentations. A structured literature-based essay investigates a focused mental-health question through explicit searching, source selection, evidence appraisal and synthesis, with optional use of PRISMA reporting tools.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: The Psychopathology course offers a deep dive into the factors shaping mental health across the lifespan. Students will develop critical thinking skills, explore the bio-psycho-social approach, and gain a comprehensive understanding of mental health and its disorders. Through key concepts, research findings, and psychological assessment techniques, this course empowers individuals to promote wellness and make a meaningful impact in both personal and professional spheres.
coursesExamined.contribution: directly studies mental health and disorders across the lifespan through biological, psychological, social and cultural perspectives; no youth-service policy or care delivery is inferred
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Provides a deep dive into factors shaping mental health. Teaches critical thinking, explores the bio‑psycho‑social approach and covers mental disorders, research findings and assessment techniques.

coursesExamined.name: Medical & Health Psychology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines health and illness through interactions among biological, psychological and sociocultural factors. Health inequalities, behaviour and prevention lead into stress, symptoms, pain, medical consultation and treatment decisions. Chronic illness is considered from patients', families' and healthcare professionals' perspectives. Students analyze research, interventions and clinical cases, practice interviewing with attention to culture, and apply clinical-health formulation to understand support and quality of life in medical settings.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Uses a biopsychosocial approach to explore how biological, psychological and socio‑cultural factors influence health and illness. Covers theories, research and interventions and focuses on the role of psychological expertise in medical settings.
coursesExamined.contribution: directly studies biopsychosocial determinants of health and illness, health behaviour, chronic illness experience and psychological expertise in medical settings
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Uses a biopsychosocial approach to explore how biological, psychological and socio‑cultural factors influence health and illness. Covers theories, research and interventions and focuses on the role of psychological expertise in medical settings.

coursesExamined.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces clinical psychological assessment and major psychotherapeutic approaches across the lifespan. Students study ethics, diagnostic systems, test reliability and validity, interviews, personality and cognitive assessment, then psychodynamic, behavioural, cognitive, humanistic, systemic and integrative treatments. Training sessions develop introductory administration, scoring and interpretation skills. A psychodiagnostic case report integrates findings and treatment recommendations, while self-monitoring examines developing clinical skills.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces key theories, methods and practices in psychodiagnostics and psychotherapy. Covers psychological assessment techniques and psychotherapeutic approaches and builds practical competencies and clinical skills.
coursesExamined.contribution: Develops psychological assessment, treatment theories, ethics, test quality and introductory administration, scoring and interpretation skills. A case report and self-monitoring develop clinical skills academically, without supervised-care qualification.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Introduces concepts, methods and ethical issues in clinical psychological assessment and psychotherapy. Students compare approaches to assessment and treatment across age groups and learn to evaluate information critically.

coursesExamined.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Teaches systematic review and meta-analysis for synthesizing evidence in medical, behavioural and related research. Students define review questions, search and select studies, extract and code findings, assess bias and compute effect sizes. Hands-on R work fits fixed- and random-effects models, examines heterogeneity and moderators, conducts meta-regression and investigates publication bias. A group project completes a small meta-analysis and presents its methods and results in a research poster.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course guides you through combining results from multiple studies using systematic reviews and meta-analysis a method now essential in psychology, medicine, social science and other disciplines. Want to know what really works? Gain hands-on skills in research synthesis that inform evidence-based policy and practice. You’ll search literature, manage data, and present findings that matter. Learn to calculate effect sizes, synthesize results and assess bias using R.
coursesExamined.contribution: Teaches systematic review, study selection, bias appraisal, effect sizes and fixed/random-effects meta-analysis in R, including heterogeneity, moderators and publication bias. A group meta-analysis and poster support evidence synthesis; this is not an independent healthcare placement.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics introduces systematic reviews and meta-analysis to synthesise results across studies. Students use R to conduct analyses, work with data structures and packages, estimate treatment effects and examine their consistency across studies. Presentations and active research tasks develop evidence-synthesis skills.

coursesExamined.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines physical, cognitive, emotional, social and personality development from prenatal life through old age and death. Biological and environmental influences are considered alongside attachment, education, relationships, cultural differences and developmental psychopathology. Students connect theoretical perspectives to case studies, assessment and interventions at different life stages. A life-story interview with an adult over fifty applies developmental concepts through interviewing, analysis and a written report.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Explores human development across the lifespan. Examines physical, cognitive, emotional and social changes from prenatal life to old age and develops critical thinking about factors influencing individual uniqueness.
coursesExamined.contribution: Studies development from prenatal life through old age and death, biological and environmental influences and case-based assessment/intervention perspectives. A life-story interview with an adult over 50 provides actual developmental inquiry; elder-care organisation is not its subject.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Explores human development across the lifespan. Examines physical, cognitive, emotional and social changes from prenatal life to old age and develops critical thinking about factors influencing individual uniqueness.

coursesExamined.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines youth radicalization and educational prevention through psychology, education, sociology, political science and peace education. Models of radicalization and adolescent risk and protective factors lead into inclusive school climates, belonging, social-emotional learning, dialogue, media literacy and civic agency. Students translate primary research into teacher-training materials and a youth toolkit for an international school project, then revise the resources using feedback from intended recipients.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Interdisciplinary course combining psychology and other social sciences in which students will have an opportunity to participate in an actual international research project and develop evidence-based materials for youth leaders and educators aimed at strengthening young people’s resilience to radicalization by promoting democratic school culture, emotionally supportive learning environments, empathy, civic engagement, and mental well-being.
coursesExamined.contribution: Examines youth radicalisation and educational prevention, risk and protective factors, belonging, inclusive school climates, social-emotional learning and civic agency. Students translate primary research into teacher-training materials and a youth toolkit, then revise using recipient feedback. This is actual youth/prevention communication work, without clinical-trial or youth-service-management equivalence.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Interdisciplinary course combining psychology and other social sciences in which students will have an opportunity to participate in an actual international research project and develop evidence-based materials for youth leaders and educators aimed at strengthening young people’s resilience to radicalization by promoting democratic school culture, emotionally supportive learning environments, empathy, civic engagement, and mental well-being.

academicJudgment: The comparator is an interdisciplinary health-services degree: actual socio-medical/public-health/health-psychology inquiry informs allocation, organisations and policy. A generic business/law/social-science combination would be insufficient. Here epidemiological needs assessment with a Zeeland health challenge, stakeholder perspectives and intervention recommendations, patient/family/professional health-psychology cases and interviewing, lifespan enquiry and explicit public-economics health/social-insurance applications materially address that substance. General legal, accounting, political and organisational courses remain complementary. The closest additionally develops disease science and empirical economics; the lifecourse programme adds actual psychopathology, introductory assessment skills, youth prevention materials and social conditions. The innovation direction retains the health-needs and evidence anchor while adding actual customer discovery, product development, market research, marketing and strategy projects. This is a related interdisciplinary response to innovation for health needs, without assuming its business projects are healthcare assignments. The business skills and health study together support the organising question; a limitation alone would not. Specialist Dutch-system, patient law, quality/insurance practice and required healthcare placement remain gaps. The insurance/markets candidate converges on the closest after retaining the health anchor and allocation/organisation tools; generic substitutions cannot create a distinct alternative.
qualitativeDistinctness: Actual health and population study anchors the programme; institutional and organisational analysis is complementary. The label avoids claiming a specialist healthcare-policy or healthcare-management degree.

The programmes share 18 courses, with 6 different courses (45 EC) in each. The closest adds biological/disease science, accounting, microeconomics and econometrics; the related programme adds social psychology and psychopathology, youth resilience, assessment practice and therapeutic approaches, modern sociology and constitutional comparison. Their organising questions differ between population/institutional analysis and development, mental health and social conditions across the lifecourse.

Five courses (37.5 EC) differ from the closest and eight (60 EC) from the lifecourse option. Startup and product development, customer insights, market research and digital strategy shift inquiry toward innovation development and adoption. The retained health-needs core makes this a related response to healthcare innovation; the business projects themselves are not guaranteed healthcare applications.
descriptionOnly: Econometrics, strategic digital transformation and market research receive full consideration within their available descriptions. Missing profiles are not a deficiency in academic eligibility. Unchanged shared modal reviews/provenance retained; current case judgments use all available workbook evidence.
alignmentFinding: All 35 UCR course identities and 11 external components occur once. Partial alignments: patient experience/health psychology; life course/development; data ethics/AI ethics; markets/microeconomics; organisations/organisational psychology; innovation/product development. The new product-design relation identifies shared user-needs/project/development work and explicitly distinguishes consumer products from healthcare innovation/business-case/implementation requirements. Other substantive study and unmatched specialist blocks retain blanks. Required 20EC organisational research differs from group meta-analysis. Optional 15EC independent research appears once per UCR column outside the 180EC and six-semester schedule, alongside required external research.
schedules: Original two programmes remain feasible. Third programme has 24 unique courses, four per semester,180EC,6 advanced courses and Year1 PPD. Every actual assigned-term X and earlier formal prerequisite read from the workbook. Methods and statistical work precede advanced synthesis; business gateway precedes strategy/research; market research precedes Consumer Product Design in its available2029h1 term. Original schedules retained; no offerings or prerequisites altered.
